intro_html: Comfort food that actually works for meal prep, with a creamy gravy that clings to tender potatoes. You get a big 49 grams of protein per bowl for about $6.61 a serving (at everyday cost). It makes 14 servings, so cook once and you are set.
cost_closing_html: About $6.61 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls delivers 49 grams of protein and about 546 calories.
upsell_html: This is the kind of dinner that feels like a treat but keeps your grocery budget right where you want it. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: The 6 lb ground beef pack is the whole ballgame here, so buy the big size and skip the small trays.
Grab plain russet or gold potatoes by the bag. An 8 lb bag runs about a buck a pound and beats anything pre-cut.
Use light sour cream to keep the fat in check without giving up the creamy texture.
make_it: Mix the ground beef with bread crumbs, a little milk, and grated onion, then roll into small meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in a large skillet until they are cooked through, working in batches if you need to.
Pour in the beef broth and let it simmer so the meatballs soak up the flavor.
Stir in the sour cream off the heat to build a smooth, creamy gravy.
Serve the meatballs and gravy over cooked potatoes and spoon extra sauce on top.
